'''Igor Rodnianski''' (born April 28, 1972, [[Ukrainian SSR]], [[Soviet Union]]) is an American mathematician at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.princeton.edu/directory/igor-rodnianski|title=Princeton Faculty Directory entry|accessdate=9 April 2016}}</ref>  He works in [[partial differential equation]]s, mathematical physics, and [[general relativity]].

==Life==

Rodnianski studied at the University of Saint Petersburg, graduating in Physics in 1996. He graduated in 1999 from [[Kansas State University]].

== Career ==

Igor Rodnianski became an instructor at Princeton in 1999. He was promoted to associate professor before 2004. 
In 2005, Dr. Rodnianski wrote paper on rough solutions to the historical Einstein Vacuum Equation with S. Klainerman.

He became full professor at Princeton in 2005. In 2011, he moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. In the Spring of 2011, he became the Henry Burchard Fine Professor of Mathematics at Princeton University.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/WebCV/RodnianskiCV.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|accessdate=9 April 2016}}</ref>

==Work==
Prof. Rodnianski specializes in [[hyperbolic partial differential equation]]s related to fundamental problems of mathematics. His work has its basis in [[geometry]], [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]], and [[mathematical physics]].  In 2002 he received the Long-Term Prize fellowship of the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]], and in 2010 the Distinguished Alumnus Award from Kansas State University.<ref name="CV"/> He received the 2011 [[Fermat Prize]] for Mathematical Research, "for fundamental contributions to the study of equations of [[general relativity]] and the propagation of light in curved space-times (with
M. Dafermos, S. Klainerman, H. Lindblad)."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/PrixFermat|title=Prix Fermat de Recherche en Mathématiques|publisher=Institut de mathématiques de Toulouse|language=French|accessdate=9 December 2011|archive-date=1 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120501061206/http://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/PrixFermat|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2017, he received a [[Simons Investigator Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-and-physical-science/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees|title=Simons Investigator Awardees|publisher=Simons Foundation|accessdate=28 July 2017|archive-date=6 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806190912/https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-and-physical-science/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2023 he was awarded the [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]] of the AMS.<ref name="Bôcher Memorial Prize 2023">{{cite web | title=2023 Bôcher Memorial Prize | website=American Mathematical Society | date=2022-12-05 | url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7133 | access-date=2024-01-15}}</ref> Also in 2023 he received the [[Clay Research Award]].<ref>[https://www.claymath.org/events/news/2023-clay-research-award Clay Research Award 2023]</ref>
